pairs.taste_axis: traditional hand-tooled plank hulls versus fast modern plywood-and-epoxy builds

lives.line: Marguerite, 64, a retired school bus driver in coastal Maine, is building a 12-foot cedar skiff alone in an unheated garage before the first snow.
lives.taste: Prefers traditional plank-on-frame work with hand tools, copper rivets, and no epoxy, even if it takes two winters.

plans.text: On day 3 she will steam four cedar ribs in a borrowed kettle and bend them into the hull while they are still hot.
On day 6 she will sharpen her drawknife and block plane and fair the stem by eye.
On day 10 she will drive copper rivets along the garboard strake with her late husband's hammer.
On day 13 she will flip the hull with two neighbors and start scraping the outside seams.

lives.line: Dev, 33, a bike courier in Seattle, is building a stitch-and-glue plywood kayak in a shared workshop so he can paddle it before the summer ends.
lives.taste: Prefers modern plywood-and-epoxy construction with jigs and power tools, valuing speed, light weight, and a launch this season.

plans.text: On day 2 he will cut the plywood panels from a kit and tape the seams with fiberglass.
On day 5 he will mix a batch of epoxy and coat the hull's interior before the workshop's evening class starts.
On day 9 he will sand the cured fillets with a random-orbit sander and fit the cockpit rim.
On day 12 he will paint the hull a flat green and test the weight against his car roof rack.

taste_ab.prompt: Which hull skin would you rather build?
options: Steam-bent cedar planks fastened with copper rivets
Stitch-and-glue plywood panels sealed with epoxy

taste_ab.prompt: Which timeline sits better with you?
options: Launch this season with a quick plywood build
Spend two winters finishing a hand-riveted hull

taste_ab.prompt: How do you want to shape the frames?
options: Hand saws and a drawknife, checked by eye
A band saw and plywood jigs for identical parts

taste_ab.prompt: What does a good Saturday at the bench look like?
options: Sharpening chisels and fitting one joint by hand
Gluing a whole panel and trimming it to shape
